question.text: Consider 5 independent Bernoulli's trials each with probability of success $\mathrm{p}$. If the probability of at least one failure is greater than or equal to $\frac{31}{32}$, then $\mathrm{p}$ lies in the interval

solution.text:
$\mathrm{n}=5$
Success $=\mathrm{p}$
Failure $=\mathrm{q}$
$\mathrm{P}$ (at least one failure) $\geq \frac{31}{32}$
$1-\mathrm{P}$ (no failure) $\geq \frac{31}{32}$
$1-\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}=5) \geq \frac{31}{32}$
$1-{ }^5 \mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{p}^5 \geq \frac{31}{32}$
$-\mathrm{p}^5 \geq-\frac{1}{32}$
$\mathrm{p}^5 \leq \frac{1}{32}$
$\mathrm{p} \leq \frac{1}{2}$
$\mathrm{p} \in\left[0, \frac{1}{2}\right]$
